entries.title: Read the kingdom pages
entries.summary: Inspect first; an action changes a particular record under a particular authority.

blocks.text: Open Village Ledger, select a known settlement, then choose Kingdom. Overview describes the government; Council lists offices and mandates; Agreements lists diplomacy; Petitions lists requests visible to you; Institutions lists recognized places; Honors lists awards; History lists committed political events.

blocks.alt: A settlement belongs to a kingdom; the kingdom's government holds the crown, and its offices are filled by people.
blocks.caption: From settlement to kingdom to government and its offices.

blocks.text: Choose Actions on a Kingdom page, or press {key:tasks} and search Government. Each supported operation has its own task and fields. Agreements, petitions, institutions, honors, offices, succession, houses, elections, and regency use separate forms rather than one generic action selector.

The server offers named records you are allowed to see. A petition remains private to its authorized viewers, ballots remain private, and another player may receive a different list. Selecting a choice does not grant authority; office, mandate, jurisdiction, current state, and installed definitions are checked again.

Consequential tasks finish on a review page showing the chosen kingdom, people, record details, and terms. Apply reviewed action performs the operation once. If government state changes while the form is open, reopen the task and review the new state.

Election and regency have dedicated tasks. Search Open a leadership election, Vote in an election, Close and count an election, Appoint a temporary regent, or End a regency. These tasks enforce the adopted constitutional rule and never infer death or incapacity from an offline or unloaded person.

entries.title: Establish a government
entries.summary: An operator, or an eligible resident, founds a kingdom's first government.

blocks.text: Founding, at a glance

blocks.alt: Check who may found the government, choose the permitted capital and constitution, review, then inspect the new government.

blocks.text: A named civic kingdom can exist without a government. Establishing one is an explicit setup action; possession of a ledger, a famous reputation, or a large Recruits army does not establish it automatically.

1. Open Establish a government. An operator chooses the named kingdom, a recognized capital settlement, an installed constitution, and an eligible first leader. With resident founding on (the default), a player whose recorded civic residence is in an ungoverned kingdom can found it too; their choices are limited to that kingdom, their residence as capital, and themselves as leader. Check whether you can found a government explains your own case. Register a missing place deliberately with settlement tasks if appropriate.

2. A civic residence is a record you register yourself: set your respawn point by sleeping in a bed inside the settlement, stand in the settlement, and open Register my residence in Kingdom Tasks (an operator or an addon can also record one). Visiting, sleeping or trading alone does not set it, and neither book creates one. The server checks the capital’s saved kingdom, the definition, the leader, and for a resident their residence again at apply time. Review all four named choices, then apply once. Establishment does not claim native territory or grant offices outside the constitution.

3. Open Overview and Council to verify the seat and leader. The profile freezes the constitutional terms used by the government. The leader can appoint offices and delegate suitable permissions. Existing social data, native claims, buildings, and troop ownership are not recreated by this step.

To move the capital later, use seat with current capital-setting authority and another eligible settlement. A capital's references must be settled before its identity is reassigned elsewhere. If a government profile is missing after a content change, affected government actions become dormant; restore the correct definition rather than bootstrapping a duplicate government.
MCA: Capitals disables MCA: Kingdoms native governance. Use the Capitals government system on such servers; installing it does not add a second working MCA: Kingdoms government alongside it.

entries.title: Appoint officials and delegate powers
entries.summary: Give a defined responsibility, not blanket control of every system.

blocks.text: An office is a defined political role. Its holder can be an eligible player or, for supported offices, a living loaded adult NPC with confirmed civic residence. The default constitution permits two offices per person in a government. Unknown adulthood or residence blocks an NPC appointment; it does not justify changing the NPC's age or home.

Open Appoint an official and choose the government, office definition, person, and any named settlement jurisdiction. Remove an official vacates that same defined scope; it does not delete or dismiss the person from ordinary life.

A leader uses Authorize a political responsibility to grant a specific responsibility to a named player and Revoke a player’s mandates to remove those grants. Every later action checks current authority again. The server carries record versions through review.

Use Council to check who actually has authority. RATIFY means permission to sign agreements for that kingdom. RECOGNIZE concerns institutions. REVIEW concerns reviewing requests. These are different from being a guild member or commanding a Recruits faction. An operator's general privilege alone does not make them a valid treaty signatory.

Appointing an NPC does not change their personal name, profession, family, schedule, needs, clothing, or AI. A temporary absence or unloaded chunk is not a vacancy. Only a confirmed applicable death event, a lawful removal, or another explicit government transition changes those records.

entries.title: Propose and sign an agreement
entries.summary: Two governments independently approve the same terms.

blocks.alt: An agreement is proposed by one kingdom, signed by an authorized holder in each of the two kingdoms, in either order, and is in force once both have signed.

nodes.label: Propose
nodes.note: The first kingdom's leader or a holder of its propose responsibility

nodes.label: Sign
nodes.note: One government's ratify holder signs the frozen terms

nodes.label: Sign
nodes.note: The other government signs the same terms

nodes.label: In force
nodes.note: Until it expires or is ended

blocks.text: You need permission to propose for the first government and a defined, available counterpart government. Start with diplomatic recognition. The bundled hospitality, scholarly exchange, craft/market charter, and civic aid agreements require active diplomatic recognition before their additional terms can take effect.

blocks.alt: Two kingdoms' banners, each pointing to one agreement scroll between them: both sign the same reviewed terms.
blocks.caption: One agreement, signed by both kingdoms.

blocks.text: 1. Open Propose an agreement, choose both named governments and an available agreement definition, then write clear terms. The proposal freezes its authored terms and duration. Read agreements to inspect the result.

2. The other authorized government opens Sign reviewed agreement terms and selects the visible proposal. The review includes its exact current terms. The server checks RATIFY authority, active governments, deadline, and frozen terms again.

3. Verify that the agreement is active. Ratified agreements become public; unratified proposals remain visible only to authorized parties. An agreement is political authorization for its supported opportunities, not a free item reward, troop transfer, building project, or teleport.

Decline rejects a proposal from the receiving side. Withdraw retracts an eligible uncompleted proposal. Terminate ends an agreement under its authority rules. Read the record before choosing, because future hospitality and other linked services can stop. Game-time expiry also ends time-limited terms.

The agreement review carries the exact current terms with the named proposal. If a stale-state message appears, reopen the task and review; never select a different record merely to get past it. Commands remain an optional technical path and require the complete hash shown by inspection.

entries.title: Ask through a petition
entries.summary: A request can be reviewed without giving its author the power to approve it.
body: Open the matching task in Kingdom Tasks: Request institution recognition, Request an honor, or Request a diplomatic introduction. Each task asks only for its real target, nominee, building, settlement, counterpart, and explanation. Named choices replace the old shared political form.

Petitions are private to the appropriate parties and review authority. A request does not immediately recognize an institution, grant an honor, transfer a kingdom, or make a treaty. It waits for review and a recorded decision.

An authorized independent reviewer may review, approve, or reject with a reason. The requester and award nominee cannot approve their own petition. Approval rechecks the original evidence, including a proposed institution's actual building. If circumstances changed, repair the prerequisite or submit a properly reviewed new request; approval is not a bypass for missing evidence.

An honor nomination produces a discretionary award, visibly different from proof of completed service. A family introduction creates an opportunity to submit an ordinary diplomatic request, not automatic treaty consent.

Withdraw is available for eligible pending requests. Expired or decided requests retain their history. Read Petitions and History to understand the result rather than repeatedly submitting duplicates; the default government limits concurrent petitions per player and kingdom.

Commission sponsorship petitions are currently disabled, even if you have completion evidence. Use the separate paid workshop and honor workflows where supported; evidence does not unlock commission petitions.

entries.title: Recognize places and honor service
entries.summary: Official status records a real place or award; it does not create one.
body: An institution is an officially recognized civic place. Available charter types come from definitions. Recognition requires the actual eligible building evidence, current political authority, and the right settlement jurisdiction. Standing at an arbitrary sign does not make it a valid workshop or institution.

Use Recognize a civic building and select where you stand or look, the government, and the available institution definition. Inspect institutions afterward. A recognized institution can support a separately chartered guild chapter and appointed contact; those remain distinct records.

Suspend recognition deliberately stops the institution's active political services without deleting its history. Revalidate checks the same original place before restoring recognition. It does not silently bind to a neighboring replacement building. A missing building provider can suspend the checks rather than inventing validity.

Honors record why a person was awarded something. An authorized discretionary honor includes a reason; a service-earned honor comes from the specific saved completion. Neither automatically grants an office, changes family history, or adds military command. Revoking an honor changes its political standing and retains the historical record.
Inspect the relevant tab before revoking or suspending. These changes can affect downstream services, even though they do not remove the actual building, NPC, or inventory.

entries.title: Plan succession before leaving office
entries.summary: A named successor is a legal choice, not automatic family inheritance.
body: A current leader opens Name a successor and chooses an eligible named person. Read overview to confirm the person before Abdicate leadership. Naming someone is not the same as immediately installing them.

Abdication vacates leadership. A government between rulers is in interregnum, meaning there is no current leader. The named successor or an authorized operator can explicitly confirm succession; eligibility is checked again. The capital, kingdom identity, and active treaties continue, while old delegated mandates do not automatically survive a leadership vacancy.

Confirmed NPC death can vacate an office. Unloading, temporary absence, and player death/respawn do not automatically install another ruler. Under the default law, Manual only, a vacancy without a named successor needs the supported operator repair or an explicitly adopted election rule, and nothing guesses an heir from family links. A kingdom that adopts a lineage law reads MCA's family records instead: see Laws of succession and heirs.

Use the House action in the current political form to record one house label, motto, and explicitly selected member for a government. This is a political record, not a surname editor or a genealogy system. Marriage never transfers the kingdom by itself.

Elections and temporary regency are explained in Evolving World. They require an adopted rule and use their own tasks in Kingdom Tasks. During an active regency the named successor is preserved; end that regency under its rules before trying to replace the protected succession arrangement.

entries.title: Laws of succession and heirs
entries.summary: A kingdom's law decides its next vacancy; Manual only, the default, changes nothing.
body: Every government starts with the law Manual only: a vacancy waits for the officials, exactly as before. Its leader or an operator can adopt another law with Adopt a law of succession, but not while a succession is under way. On the Kingdom page, Succession shows the law and the succession under way; members of the court also see who would succeed now and why.

Named heir, then lineage puts the named successor first, then the ruler's children, grandchildren and siblings as MCA's family tree records them. Equal inheritance reads the same relatives without a named successor. Council confirmation adds the council's confirmation. Elective monarchy leaves every vacancy to the government's elections. Relatives come in a fixed order by person, because MCA records no birth order: nothing is random and no gender is read.

When the ruler's death is observed, or the ruler abdicates or is removed, one succession opens and is decided within a few seconds. An NPC heir who is an adult resident of the kingdom is seated. A player heir is offered the crown and answers with Answer an offered crown. A minor heir waits under a regency until verified adulthood: a living player parent governs as regent when the kingdom's transition rule allows regencies; otherwise an operator appoints one.

An elected ruler is never replaced by lineage, and a successor the government elected always comes first. When evidence cannot be verified, such as a villager that is not loaded or a missing family record, the succession waits instead of guessing and asks again when it can. Review a succession lets an official or operator ask the law again or leave the succession to the officials. Kingdoms whose crown MCA Capitals governs are never decided here.

entries.title: Court titles, claims and mourning
entries.summary: Ranks are ceremonial; a claim changes the succession only by the crown's recorded decision.
body: An official with the Award honors responsibility grants court ranks with Grant a court title. Each kingdom names its ranks in its own style. A rank is ceremonial: it grants no office, permission, Recruits command or Crime privilege. A player accepts an offered rank first and may resign it with honor; a landed rank names one settlement of the kingdom.

Someone in the line of succession may renounce their place. A player may file a claim with the crown: contest the order, ask to be recognized as a member of the ruling house, or ask for a renounced place back. An official who appoints, or an operator, decides it, never the claimant. Every decision is kept, and a dismissed claim may be filed again after a wait.

Legitimacy is a reading of the ruler's claim from a few bounded records: how they were seated, a verified family tie, the council's confirmation, agreements in force, a seated council and open contests. It changes no authority. The court sees its reasons; everyone else sees the level.

When a ruler's death is observed, the kingdom mourns for a day: its pages say so and its banners darken. Nothing changes on any villager or player. A memorial records each reign that ended by death or abdication.

entries.title: Banners, seals and charters
entries.summary: A charter is official only while the ledger holds what it proves.

blocks.text: Kingdom banners, heraldic shields and court noticeboards stand for the kingdom where they are placed: the settlement they stand in or, outside settlements, the placer's residence. They show the kingdom's colours and sigil, and its leader chooses the colours with Choose your kingdom's colours. Use a noticeboard to read the kingdom's latest proclamations and public records.

blocks.alt: The kingdom's banner, then a seal press, then a charter with a red seal: a charter is sealed at a press for a record of the kingdom.
blocks.caption: Arms, seal press, sealed charter.

blocks.text: An official seals a charter at a seal press: hold a blank charter within 4 blocks of the press and open Seal a charter. A proclamation needs Award honors, an office appointment Appoint officials and a treaty Ratify agreements; the leader seals the founding. The ledger records the document first; then the charter carries it.

Use a charter, or Inspect a charter, to ask the ledger. It is official while what it proves holds, official but historical once that no longer holds, revoked after Revoke a sealed document, and unverified when no sealed record matches it, as with an altered copy or one from another world. A charter proves a record; it never grants authority by itself.

entries.title: Read history and private records
entries.summary: A history entry tells you what was committed, and who may see it.
body: Open the History tab from the kingdom screen. Entries show a recorded political action, its game-day timing, attribution, and current status. History is read-only; selecting an entry is not a way to repeat its original action.

Current means the recorded result still has that standing. Superseded means a later decision replaced or progressed it. Expired means its time-limited effect has ended. The old event remains historical even when its present effect changes.

Public facts can be visible broadly. Private petitions are restricted to involved people and current authorized reviewers; unratified agreements are restricted to their parties. Individual ballots are private to the voter. Knowing a record name or sharing a settlement does not make a private record yours to read.

The server records committed decisions before publishing the associated notice. This supports stable replay and restart behavior, but history is not a promise that every optional mod maintains a second archive. The supported Townstead version has no separate Chronicles archive adapter.

For a changed or disputed outcome, use the current live record and its lawful review, termination, or recovery path. Removing a history file is not a safe undo: a quest payment, troop handoff, or another provider's saved state may already exist.

entries.title: Political notices and office badges
entries.summary: Optional notices of public political moments, and a line naming nearby officials.

blocks.text: Political notices tell you about public moments in the committed political record: a government founded, a leader or official taking office, an office falling vacant, and a memorial when an official's death is confirmed. Each moment is shown once, in neutral words: an office keeps the name its constitution gives it, and no one is said to be crowned. Notices are off until you turn them on.

Open Settings from Kingdom Tasks and choose the Politics tab. Political notices: Off shows none, Chat line adds one line to chat, and Chat line and banner also shows a short banner. No sound plays and nothing interrupts what you are doing; the chat line is the text version of the banner.

Only public facts are announced. Private mandates, proposals, ballots and consent never are. A local office is announced only to players who know its settlement. A person who is merely offline or in an unloaded area is never reported dead.

Office badges are a small line above a public office holder near you naming their office: ♛ marks a leader, ⚑ another office, and +N how many more they hold. The person's own name, custom name, skin and equipment never change, and no office is guessed from a name. Badges follow appointments, dismissals and successions and are dropped when the person leaves your view or you disconnect. The Politics tab hides them or sets how far away they show (4 to 48 blocks, 16 by default).
Kingdom Tasks' person pickers and the council list also name each person's public offices. A server operator can turn notices or badges off for everyone; then the settings have nothing to show.
